theorem.name: FINITE_GROUPOID_COMPONENT_FIXED_POINT_CRITERION
theorem.statement: For a finite groupoid Gamma and a finite candidate functor C:Gamma->FinSet, natural selections 1=>C are in canonical bijection with the product over connected-component representatives M_i of C(M_i)^{Aut(M_i)}.
theorem.consequence: Pointwise nonempty candidate fibers do not imply a natural selection; a component with no automorphism-fixed candidate kills every global natural selection.

strength_separation.unique_object: candidate fiber has exactly one element
strength_separation.unique_isomorphism_class: candidate action groupoid has exactly one orbit; this does not imply an automorphism-fixed representative
strength_separation.fixed_point: candidate is fixed by every primitive-preserving automorphism of the model
strength_separation.natural_section: a coherent candidate family on the model groupoid; on each connected component this is equivalent to an automorphism-fixed candidate at one representative

checker_spec.name: FINITE_NATURALITY_CHECKER_V1
inputs: verified candidate transport functor on model isomorphisms
validation: validate each automorphism image as a finite group action
compute candidate orbit partitions and stabilizers
for explicit multi-object groupoids validate transport identity/composition/inverse laws
report natural-selection count as product of fixed-point counts over component representatives
checker_spec.hard_boundary: The checker cannot invent the primitive-preserving automorphism group, candidate transport, or symmetry-breaking datum; those must be declared or derived from the model.
